tsu-109-student-scientific-conference-20.about:
The 'TSU 109' Student Scientific Conference is organised every year by the Faculty of Humanities of Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University to mark the university's founding; the 2027 edition is the fifth. It takes place at TSU in Tbilisi on 11-12 February 2027.

Students send a thesis (abstract) of at most one page (about 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) together with a written statement from a professor or supervisor confirming it meets the conference's academic requirements. Accepted speakers present for 15 minutes, followed by 10 minutes of discussion. The working language is Georgian.

It is a first step into academic presenting for undergraduate and master's students, and a line on a CV that graduate programmes and scholarship committees value.
highlights: Annual conference tied to TSU's founding anniversary
tsu-109-student-scientific-conference-20.eligibility: Students able to present research in Georgian, with a supporting statement from a professor or supervisor. The announcement is addressed to TSU students and does not say whether students of other universities are accepted; ask the organisers.
how_to_apply: Write a one-page abstract (max. 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 line spacing)
Get a written statement from your professor or supervisor approving the abstract
Email both to javakhishvili_students@tsu.ge by 20 December 2026
If accepted, present on 11-12 February 2027 at TSU (contact: Dr Nino Popiashvili)

tsu-art-history-student-conference-2026.about:
The Institute of the History and Theory of Art at Ivane Javakhishvili Tbilisi State University is holding the student conference 'Man and Culture Across Epochs' at TSU on 26-27 December 2026. The programme will be published from 11 December.

It is open to bachelor's and master's students and recent graduates from any university. Applicants email an abstract of up to 300 words (with name, year of study and field before the text; Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) plus a written recommendation from a supervisor. Each accepted paper gets a 15-minute slot and 5 minutes of questions. The working language is Georgian.

For students of art history, cultural studies, history or humanities it is an accessible first conference presentation, with a short abstract and a quick turnaround.
highlights: Open to students from any university
tsu-art-history-student-conference-2026.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students and recent graduates from any university who can present in Georgian. A supervisor's recommendation is required.
how_to_apply: Write an abstract of up to 300 words; put your name, year of study and field before the text
Get a written recommendation or conclusion from your supervisor
Email both to tsuarthistoryconference@gmail.com by 10 November 2026
Check the programme from 11 December and present on 26-27 December 2026

tsu-career-orientation-senior-pupils-202.about:
TSU's Child University runs career-orientation sessions for senior pupils (grades 10, 11 and 12) from both public and private schools. The sessions answer questions about choosing a profession, university news, TSU's bachelor's programmes and admission requirements in Georgia's national exam system.

Sessions can be held physically at TSU or remotely. Schools or pupils register through a Google form; TSU also runs a Facebook group for admission information.

Useful for any pupil deciding between subjects and universities, and especially for those targeting Georgia's largest public university.
highlights: Covers TSU programmes and admission rules
tsu-career-orientation-senior-pupils-202.eligibility: Pupils in grades 10-12 at public or private schools in Georgia. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Open the TSU Child University announcement
Fill in the Google registration form
Optionally join the TSU Child University Facebook group for admission updates
Wait for TSU to confirm the session date

tsu-day-at-tsu-school-visits.about:
Day at TSU (დღე თსუში) and the related Visiting TSU (სტუმრად თსუში) offer give school classes a free guided tour of Tbilisi State University: its historic First Building museum (Wednesdays), the historic library (Mondays or Thursdays), the planetarium in the Second Building (Tuesdays), the Mineralogy Museum (Fridays), and selected laboratories.

Visits are for one class at a time, up to 30 pupils, and are arranged by a teacher or tutor, who fills in the online registration form and is then contacted by TSU to confirm the day and time.

A free and easy way for a school club or class to see a university, planetarium and science museum up close.
highlights: Free; up to 30 pupils per visit
Planetarium, museums, historic library and labs
Booked by a teacher via online form
tsu-day-at-tsu-school-visits.eligibility: School classes from any grade, booked by a teacher or tutor. Tours in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Teacher opens the 'Visiting TSU' announcement
Chooses a venue and weekday and fills in the Google form
Waits for TSU's call or message confirming the date
Brings the class (max 30 pupils) to TSU Building I, 1 Chavchavadze Ave

tsu-erasmus-plus-exchange-scholarships-2.about:
Through Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility (funded by the European Commission) and bilateral agreements, Tbilisi State University sends students from all seven faculties to partner universities in Europe. Each call lists the available places by country, university and subject; applicants may apply to up to three universities per call.

Erasmus+ grants cover a monthly allowance set by the EU for the host country plus a travel contribution, and tuition is waived at the host. Separate calls exist for doctoral students and for specific partners. TSU's International Relations Department publishes all calls on its 'Current exchange' page with deadlines and document lists; questions go to outgoingmobility@tsu.ge (Erasmus+) or exchange@tsu.ge (bilateral).
highlights: EU-funded semester abroad with monthly allowance and travel grant
Calls several times a year for all study levels
Apply to up to three partner universities per call
tsu-erasmus-plus-exchange-scholarships-2.eligibility: Active TSU bachelor's, master's and PhD students meeting each call's GPA and language requirements (international certificates or TSU's institutional language test).
how_to_apply: Check TSU's 'Current exchange' page regularly for new calls.
Pick up to three partner universities from the call's list.
Prepare transcript, motivation letter, language certificate (or TSU institutional test result) and learning agreement draft.
Register and upload documents before the call deadline; attend interviews if invited.
tsu-erasmus-plus-exchange-scholarships-2.costs: Erasmus+: EU monthly allowance (country-dependent) + travel support, host tuition waived. Bilateral: per partner agreement.

tsu-humanities-9th-student-conference-20.about:
TSU's Faculty of Humanities holds its ninth student conference on 17-18 December 2026 to support student research, interdisciplinary work and interest in Georgian studies. Sections include history, ethnology, archaeology, Georgian studies, Caucasology, translation studies, Western European languages and literature, American studies, oriental studies, Slavic and Russian studies, philosophy, cultural studies, art and interdisciplinary research.

Applicants email an application and a one-page abstract (max. 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) with a written statement from a professor or supervisor. Presentations are in person: 15 minutes plus 5 minutes of discussion, in Georgian.

It is a low-stakes, well-organised setting for humanities students to give their first conference paper.
tsu-humanities-9th-student-conference-20.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students of TSU's Faculty of Humanities. Working language: Georgian.
how_to_apply: Prepare a one-page abstract (max. 250 words, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing)
Get a written statement from a professor or supervisor
Email the application and abstract to hs@tsu.ge by 15 November 2026
Questions: nino.popiashvili@tsu.ge (Room 204, 1 Chavchavadze Ave.)

tsu-junior-schools-child-university.about:
The Junior Schools (ნორჩთა სკოლები) are part of TSU's Child University, Georgia's oldest university outreach programme for school pupils. They are aimed at pupils who want to explore academic subjects beyond the regular curriculum, with university staff and students.

Five strands run: the Junior Astronomers School, Junior Economists School, Junior Humanists School, the Law Club and the Geography Club. Pupils from public and private schools in grades 7-12 can take part. TSU does not publish a timetable or fee on the page; enrol by emailing junior@tsu.ge or calling +995 32 2 25 04 84.

A strong extracurricular for olympiad preparation (astronomy, economics, geography) and for pupils who want early contact with university departments.
highlights: Taught by TSU staff and students
tsu-junior-schools-child-university.eligibility: Pupils in grades 7-12 at Georgian public or private schools. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Read the Junior Schools page on tsu.ge
Email junior@tsu.ge or call +995 32 2 25 04 84 naming the club you want
Follow the TSU Child University news page for club registration posts
tsu-junior-schools-child-university.costs: Not stated on the page; ask TSU when enrolling.

tsu-language-of-cinema-teen-course-2026.about:
The Language of Cinema: Story, Vision, Creativity is an educational and creative course run by TSU's Child University for teenagers aged 12-17. It is taught by filmmaker and educator Nino Gelovani and explores how films tell stories, how images and framing create meaning, and how young people can develop their own creative ideas for the screen.

The course lasts 12 weeks, with sessions every Friday at 17:00 starting on 23 October 2026, at Tbilisi State University. Registration is through an online form linked on the TSU page; places are limited. Questions go to junior@tsu.ge.

A rare structured film course for teenagers, useful for anyone building an arts or media portfolio.
highlights: Storytelling, visual language and creative practice
tsu-language-of-cinema-teen-course-2026.eligibility: Teenagers aged 12-17. Taught in Georgian at TSU, Tbilisi.
how_to_apply: Open the TSU Child University announcement
Fill in the Google registration form linked there
Because the course started on 23 October, email junior@tsu.ge to confirm a place is still available
Attend Fridays at 17:00
tsu-language-of-cinema-teen-course-2026.costs: The page does not state a fee; contact junior@tsu.ge to confirm.

tsu-library-childrens-conference-inanish.about:
Tbilisi State University's Library runs a children's events series, 'University Library for Children'. Its next event is a conference for pupils of public and private schools in Georgia dedicated to the 100th anniversary of the birth of the Georgian writer Revaz Inanishvili, with presentations on his work.

Pupils submit an abstract of up to 250 words (one A4 page, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing) by 9 November 2026. Selected authors are told by 16 November and send their final papers by 1 December; the conference date will be announced afterwards. The working language is Georgian, and the email must name the pupil, the school and the supervising teacher.

It gives secondary-school students a rare chance to present literary research at a university, which is good preparation for academic writing and a strong line on a university application.
highlights: Pupils present at Tbilisi State University
Free, with a teacher as supervisor
tsu-library-childrens-conference-inanish.eligibility: Pupils of public and private schools in Georgia, writing and presenting in Georgian, supported by a teacher.
how_to_apply: Write an abstract of up to 250 words on Revaz Inanishvili's work (one A4 page, Sylfaen 12, 1.5 spacing)
Email it by 9 November 2026 to khatuna.galdava@tsu.ge and khatuna.chugoshvili@tsu.ge with your full name, school, teacher's name and contact details
If selected (by 16 November), send the full paper by 1 December 2026
Present at TSU on the date the library announces (questions: 577 955 855)

ug-mathematics-olympiad-grades-5-12-2027.about:
The University of Georgia (UG) holds an annual mathematics olympiad for pupils in grades 5 to 12; the 2026 edition was the third. Participation is completely free and the olympiad takes place at UG's Building IV, 77a Kostava Street, Tbilisi.

In 2026 the announcement came out on 5 March with registration open until 31 March; registered pupils were told the exact date in advance. Top scorers receive prizes and commemorative gifts from the university.

A low-stakes, free olympiad that gives younger pupils competition practice before the national olympiad rounds.
ug-mathematics-olympiad-grades-5-12-2027.eligibility: Pupils in grades 5-12. Problems in Georgian.
how_to_apply: Watch ug.edu.ge announcements for the 2027 call (expected March)
Register on the UG mathematics olympiad page before the deadline
Wait for UG to send the olympiad date
Sit the olympiad at UG Building IV, 77a Kostava St

undp-ohchr-human-rights-winter-school-ge.about:
The Human Rights Winter School is organised by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) within the EU-UN joint project 'Human Rights for All'. It runs from 29 November to 4 December 2026 and covers human rights in a democratic society, human-rights protection institutions and their challenges, freedom of expression, the right to privacy and personal-data protection.

The programme mixes lectures, discussions, presentations and group exercises, with practical work on communication and presentation skills. It is for students and recent graduates aged 18-24 from law, social sciences, political science and humanities programmes at accredited Georgian universities; applicants from regional universities are particularly welcome. Teaching is in Georgian.

Organisers fully cover transport and accommodation, and everyone who completes the programme gets a certificate, which makes it a strong, free addition to a CV for careers in law, policy or international organisations.
highlights: Fully funded: transport and accommodation covered
Run by UNDP and OHCHR with EU funding
undp-ohchr-human-rights-winter-school-ge.eligibility: Students and graduates aged 18-24 of law, social sciences, political sciences or humanities at accredited higher-education institutions in Georgia, with good Georgian and able to attend the whole programme. Regional-university applicants are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Prepare a CV and a motivation letter of no more than 300 words (your human-rights experience, why you want to attend, how you will use it)
Complete the registration form linked from the EU in Georgia announcement
Submit before 10 November 2026
Shortlisted applicants are contacted by UNDP (contact: ana.kvernadze@undp.org)
undp-ohchr-human-rights-winter-school-ge.costs: Free. Transport and accommodation are fully covered by the organisers.

university-of-georgia-funding-2027.about:
The University of Georgia (UG), a large private university in Tbilisi, publishes an annual funding package for UNE entrants. Full funding: a competitive score of 2,050 or more gives full funding on any bachelor's programme; technology-programme entrants with 2,100+ also receive a laptop. Future Support Grant: scores of 2,000–2,049 receive full funding in exchange for an income-share commitment (graduates contribute 25% of their income to fund future students, per UG's rules).

UG also offers 50% targeted funding for internally displaced persons from the occupied territories, 50% co-funding for UG School graduates, and a performance scholarship for the top 3% of students by GPA.
highlights: 100% tuition for 2,050+ UNE scores (+ laptop for 2,100+ in tech)
50% targeted funding for IDPs; top-3% GPA scholarship
university-of-georgia-funding-2027.eligibility: Applicants entering UG bachelor's programmes via the 2027 Unified National Exams; IDP funding requires official IDP status; performance scholarship for current UG students.
how_to_apply: Register for the 2027 Unified National Exams.
Choose a UG bachelor's programme in the NAEC system.
Reach the score threshold; funding is applied on enrolment (read the Future Support Grant terms carefully before accepting).
IDP applicants submit status documents to UG.
university-of-georgia-funding-2027.costs: Full tuition (100%) or 50% reductions depending on scheme; the Future Support Grant carries a post-graduation income-share obligation.

youth-palace-chess-school-2026-27.about:
The Chess School of the National Palace of Youth is one of Tbilisi's long-standing chess clubs. For 2026-27 it offers groups for ages 5-17 at several levels (beginners in their 2nd-3rd year, ranked players, amateurs and advanced, the last for ages 5-14) at 80 GEL a month, and a selective enhanced group for strong players at 150 GEL a month. Adult groups are also available.

Registration is online; coordinator Maia Bokuchava (598 180 979) advises on levels.

Structured coaching for children who want to compete in national youth chess events.
youth-palace-chess-school-2026-27.eligibility: Children and teenagers aged 5-17 (adult groups also). Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Read the direction page on youthpalace.ge
Register online at registration.youthpalace.ge
Call the direction coordinator to confirm a group and schedule
Attend sessions at the Palace, 6 Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi
youth-palace-chess-school-2026-27.costs: 80 GEL/month (preparatory groups); 150 GEL/month (enhanced and adult groups).

youth-palace-engineering-clubs-2026-27.about:
Alongside robotics, the Palace's Architecture and Engineering direction runs a wide range of hands-on technical clubs for 2026-27: Radioelectronics (grades 5-12), Aeromodelling (grades 2-12), Wood Product Making (grades 2-12), Engineering Graphics (grades 7-11), Architecture (grades 7-12) and Computer Graphics (grades 6-12, covering Photoshop, Illustrator, CorelDRAW, AutoCAD, ArchiCAD and 3ds Max).

Group fees are 60 GEL a month (individual lessons 150 GEL). There is also a free Engineering Technical Corner with selective admission, and an engineering-graphics entrance-exam course for ages 16+. Registration is online; the coordinator confirms groups.

Rare in-person maker clubs that help pupils build a portfolio for architecture, design or engineering degrees.
highlights: Architecture and CAD software (AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, 3ds Max)
youth-palace-engineering-clubs-2026-27.eligibility: School pupils by club (grades 2-12); some adult groups. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Read the direction page on youthpalace.ge
Register online at registration.youthpalace.ge (upload the registration-fee receipt where required)
Call the direction coordinator to confirm a group and schedule
Attend sessions at the Palace, 6 Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi
youth-palace-engineering-clubs-2026-27.costs: Group clubs 60 GEL/month; individual 150 GEL/month; Engineering Technical Corner free (selective).

youth-palace-film-studios-2026-27.about:
The Audio-Visual direction of the National Palace of Youth runs two free film programmes for 2026-27: the amateur film studio 'Pioneer Film' (პიონერფილმი) for ages 12-17 and 'First Steps in Cinema' for ages 8-11. Members learn filmmaking by doing, and the Palace also hosts the international youth film festival 'Taoba', where young filmmakers screen their work.

A photography circle for ages 12-17 is also available at 70 GEL a month. Registration is online; coordinator Maia Landia (577 777 871) confirms groups.

A free way for children and teenagers to start making films and build a creative portfolio.
highlights: Free film studios for ages 8-11 and 12-17
Linked to the 'Taoba' youth film festival
youth-palace-film-studios-2026-27.eligibility: Children aged 8-11 and teenagers aged 12-17. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Read the direction page on youthpalace.ge
Register online at registration.youthpalace.ge
Call the direction coordinator to confirm a group and schedule
Attend sessions at the Palace, 6 Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi
youth-palace-film-studios-2026-27.costs: Film studios free; photography circle 70 GEL/month.

youth-palace-olympiad-mathematics-club-2.about:
The Mathematics and Modern Technologies direction of the National Palace of Youth offers a free Olympiad Mathematics group for strong pupils, with admission by preliminary selection, aimed at preparing for national and international mathematics olympiads.

The same direction runs paid options for 2026-27: a Programming Circle (front-end, JavaScript and Python) from grade 5 at 80 GEL a month, a Mathematics and Programming Weekend School for grades 5-7 (100 GEL a month), and a general mathematics circle for grades 1-11 (60 GEL). It also offers free Aflatoun/Aflateen social and financial education groups for ages 9-16.

The free olympiad group is one of the few no-cost structured olympiad-training options in Tbilisi; contact coordinator Nana Shengelia (599 16 63 13) to arrange the selection.
youth-palace-olympiad-mathematics-club-2.eligibility: Olympiad group: pupils who pass the preliminary selection (roughly grades 5-12). Programming circle from grade 5. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Read the direction page on youthpalace.ge
Register online at registration.youthpalace.ge (upload the registration-fee receipt where required)
Call the direction coordinator to confirm a group and schedule
Attend sessions at the Palace, 6 Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi
youth-palace-olympiad-mathematics-club-2.costs: Olympiad mathematics: free. Programming circle 80 GEL/month; weekend school 100 GEL/month; maths circle 60 GEL/month.

youth-palace-robotics-clubs-2026-27.about:
The National Palace of Youth on Rustaveli Avenue is Tbilisi's largest centre for after-school clubs, with more than 160 circles. Its Architecture and Engineering direction runs a ladder of robotics programmes for 2026-27: Logo-robotics for ages 4-6, Robotics and Coding for grades 2-5, My First Robots for ages 11+ (admission by interview), and an advanced Robotics Engineering course for ages 14-17 (selective).

Groups meet weekly through the school year. Fees are monthly: 60 GEL (Logo-robotics), 80 GEL (Robotics and Coding), 100 GEL (My First Robots) and 150 GEL (advanced course). Registration is online, and the direction coordinator (Nargiz Chkadua, 551 08 99 43) confirms groups and schedules.

A structured, affordable route from first robots to competition-level engineering, suitable for pupils who want to join FLL-style teams or study engineering.
youth-palace-robotics-clubs-2026-27.eligibility: Children and teenagers by level: ages 4-6, grades 2-5, ages 11+ (interview), ages 14-17 (selective). Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Read the direction page on youthpalace.ge
Register online at registration.youthpalace.ge (upload the registration-fee receipt where required)
Call the direction coordinator to confirm a group and schedule
Attend sessions at the Palace, 6 Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi
youth-palace-robotics-clubs-2026-27.costs: Monthly fees: 60-150 GEL depending on the group.

youth-palace-school-research-conference-.about:
The National Palace of Youth runs an annual school research conference (სასწავლო-კვლევითი კონფერენცია) for pupils aged 12-18 from any public or private school in Georgia. It encourages research, experiments, inventions, engineering models and prototypes, and builds research, public-speaking and presentation skills. The 2026 theme was 'The Digital Era and Its Challenges'.

Sections cover linguistics and literature, mathematics, history, geography, chemistry, biology, physics, programming and modern technologies, engineering and architecture, and civic education. In 2026, submissions ran from 9 February to 16 March, evaluation through April, results on 23 April (with an appeal window) and the awards ceremony on 16 May. Expect a similar calendar in 2027; the rules are published as a regulation on the project page.

A free, nationwide platform for a first research project, useful for olympiad-minded pupils and for university applications.
highlights: Open to pupils aged 12-18 across Georgia
Ten subject sections incl. programming and engineering
Free to enter, awards in May
youth-palace-school-research-conference-.eligibility: Pupils aged 12-18 at public or private schools in Georgia. Georgian-language.
how_to_apply: Check the conference page on youthpalace.ge from January 2027 for the new regulation
Choose a section and prepare your research or prototype
Submit within the window (2026: 9 Feb-16 Mar)
Await results (late April) and the awards ceremony (May)

youth-palace-science-circles-2026-27.about:
The Palace's Natural and Social Sciences direction runs weekly circles for the 2026-27 school year: Biology (grades 7-11), Chemistry (8-11), Physics (7-11), History (7-11), Geography (7-11) and Nature Studies (3-6), each at 60 GEL a month. A Psychology group for grades 9-12 is free, and a Science Corner with selective admission is also free.

For older pupils there are entrance-exam preparation groups (ages 16+, 150 GEL) and small-group tutoring. Registration is online; coordinator Nino Kikabidze (599 899 734) confirms groups.

Good for pupils who want more lab-style science than school offers, or a base for subject olympiads.
highlights: Free psychology group and Science Corner
Central Tbilisi, weekly through the year
how_to_apply: Read the direction page on youthpalace.ge
Register online at registration.youthpalace.ge (upload the registration-fee receipt where required)
Call the direction coordinator to confirm a group and schedule
Attend sessions at the Palace, 6 Rustaveli Avenue, Tbilisi
youth-palace-science-circles-2026-27.costs: Circles 60 GEL/month; psychology and Science Corner free; exam prep 150 GEL/month.

42-abu-dhabi-coding-school.about:
42 Abu Dhabi is a member of the 42 Network of coding schools. Learning is peer-to-peer, project-based and gamified: there are no lectures or teachers, students progress through coding projects at their own pace, and the school describes itself as the first accredited academy of its kind in the GCC, with a Level 6 qualification equivalent to a bachelor's in software development and AI applications.

Admission has three steps: pass the online game (logic and memory), attend a check-in, and survive 'The Piscine', an intensive four-week coding bootcamp that serves as the final selection. Piscines are held in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain; dates are posted on the Piscine Status page.

Tuition is free and no coding experience is needed; the only stated requirement is being 18. Living costs are not covered.
42-abu-dhabi-coding-school.eligibility: Anyone aged 18+; no coding experience or degree required (check residency/visa requirements with the school).
how_to_apply: Create an account on apply.42abudhabi.ae
Pass the online game
Book a check-in
Join the next Piscine (Abu Dhabi or Al Ain) and complete it
42-abu-dhabi-coding-school.costs: Tuition-free; living and travel costs are the student's own.

abu-dhabi-university-scholarship-uae-gcc.about:
Abu Dhabi University, one of the UAE's largest private universities with campuses in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain and Dubai, runs seven scholarship categories. The University Scholarship gives a 15% to 50% waiver on tuition fees for UAE residents and GCC candidates (GCC candidates must provide officially attested documents). Continuing students can earn an Academic Scholarship (20%) or Athletic Scholarship (25%), and postgraduate applicants with an undergraduate CGPA of at least 3.5 receive a 25% Merit-based Graduate Scholarship.

Awards last up to four years or until graduation. After admission, the student logs into the ADU account where all scholarships they qualify for appear, and applies online.
highlights: 15–50% tuition waiver for UAE residents and GCC applicants
abu-dhabi-university-scholarship-uae-gcc.eligibility: Admitted ADU students who are UAE residents or GCC nationals (with attested documents) and meet the merit criteria; graduate merit waiver requires an undergraduate CGPA ≥ 3.5.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to ADU and obtain your student ID.
Log in to your ADU account and open the Financial Aid and Scholarships section.
Apply online for the scholarships shown as available to you and upload any documents.
Meet the maintenance criteria each year to keep the award.

abu-dhabi-university-sheikh-hamdan-schol.about:
Named after H.H. Sheikh Hamdan Bin Zayed Al Nahyan, this is Abu Dhabi University's fully funded undergraduate scholarship: a 100% waiver on tuition, application fee, registration fee, student services fee and health service fee, for up to four years or until graduation.

As with all ADU scholarships, students do not submit a separate pre-admission form: once admitted, scholarships the student is eligible for, based on their academic record, appear in the ADU account and can be applied for online.
abu-dhabi-university-sheikh-hamdan-schol.eligibility: Outstanding students admitted to ADU bachelor's programmes who meet the award's merit criteria (shown in the student account after admission); check nationality rules with ADU admissions.
how_to_apply: Apply for admission to an ADU bachelor's programme with your best grades.
After admission, check your ADU account for the Sheikh Hamdan Bin Zayed Scholarship.
Complete the online application and upload documents.
Maintain the academic criteria every year.
abu-dhabi-university-sheikh-hamdan-schol.costs: 100% waiver on tuition, application, registration, student services and health service fees.

ajmi-media-skills-for-youth.about:
The Al Jazeera Media Institute (AJMI) runs a 'Media Skills for Youth' category alongside its professional training. Upcoming courses include TV Presentation Skills for Youth (ages 9-15; in English or Arabic, 20-24 December 2026), Voice Placement for Youth (20-22 December), Little Entrepreneur (27-29 December, English) and Story Writing for Youth (27-29 December). Classes take place in AJMI's studios in Doha and use real studio equipment such as teleprompters and microphones.

Courses suit students curious about journalism, presenting and storytelling. Registration is online through an AJMI account; fees are around QAR 1,000 per 5-day course.
highlights: Taught by Al Jazeera trainers in real studios
ajmi-media-skills-for-youth.eligibility: Children and teenagers (each course lists its age group, e.g. 9-15) able to attend in Doha.
how_to_apply: Open the AJMI courses page and filter by "Media Skills for Youth"
Create an account on the AJMI site
Register and pay for the course
Attend the evening sessions in Doha
ajmi-media-skills-for-youth.costs: About QAR 1,000 (USD 274) for a 5-day youth course; shorter courses cost less.

apg-mun-vi-2026.about:
APG MUN is the Model United Nations conference of the Arabian Pearl Gulf School in Bahrain. Its sixth edition takes place on 4–5 December 2026. Councils include UNICEF, WHO, UN Women, the ILO and the UN Security Council, an Arabic-language Arab Strategic Affairs Council and specialised councils such as the International Criminal Court.

All high-school students and first-year university students can attend. Delegates register on apgmun.com (status 'pending'), pay, receive an invoice and are then confirmed; special roles can be requested afterwards.

A bilingual Gulf conference that is a good entry point for students in Bahrain and the Eastern Province.
highlights: High school and first-year university students
apg-mun-vi-2026.eligibility: High-school students and first-year university students. English and Arabic committees.
how_to_apply: Create an account at apgmun.com/register
Complete the delegate registration (status pending)
Pay and receive your invoice to be confirmed
Apply for special positions if wanted and attend 4–5 December
apg-mun-vi-2026.costs: Delegate fee invoiced after registration on the official portal; travel and accommodation extra.

aubh-international-scholarships-2027.about:
The American University of Bahrain is a US-style university in Riffa offering engineering, business, design and computing degrees taught in English. Its scholarships for international students include the Global Scholarship, President's Scholarship, Early Enrollees Award, the Inspire, Lead and Compete Award, and sibling and alumni discounts.

Awards are discretionary and limited. You must indicate scholarship interest on the application form and submit documents through the Scholarship Support Form. For Spring 2027 entry applications are due 27 Dec 2026 with results by 7 Jan 2027; Fall 2027 dates will follow.
highlights: Global and President's Scholarships for internationals
aubh-international-scholarships-2027.eligibility: International applicants to AUBH bachelor's programmes; awards based on merit, leadership and talent.
how_to_apply: Apply to AUBH and tick scholarship interest on the form
Submit the Scholarship Support Form with documents
Spring 2027: by 27 Dec 2026; Fall 2027: check AUBH dates
aubh-international-scholarships-2027.costs: Partial to full tuition depending on award (discretionary).

aud-pre-university-summer-camp-2027.about:
AUD's pre-university Summer Camp gives Grade 10–11 (Year 11–12) students a taste of university life in Dubai. Students choose one track: Empowered Leadership; Tech Pioneers (AI, game design, robotics and VR); Master the Power of Media; Life-Lab (biology and pre-med); or Creative Lab (design and branding with AI).

The fee covers accommodation, meals, excursions, local transport, modules, on-campus activities and some airport transfers, so it suits international students; insurance, visas and flights are not included. 2027 dates are to be announced.

Apply with your preferred track, country, grade, latest report card and passport copy; AUD then sends next steps and pricing.
highlights: Five tracks from AI to pre-med
aud-pre-university-summer-camp-2027.eligibility: Students currently in Grade 10–11 (Year 11–12), any nationality.
how_to_apply: Open summercamp.aud.edu
Fill in the Apply Now form (track, country, grade)
Upload your report card and passport copy
Wait for AUD's next-step email with dates and fees
aud-pre-university-summer-camp-2027.costs: Fee on request; covers accommodation, meals, excursions, transport and activities; flights, visa and insurance extra.

ciee-january-in-abu-dhabi-2027.about:
CIEE January in Abu Dhabi is a short winter-break programme running 28 December 2026 – 17 January 2027 (tentative). Students take one 3-credit course taught in person in English at CIEE Abu Dhabi, combined with cultural activities in the UAE capital.

It requires a 2.50 GPA and no language background. The fee is USD 3,950 including housing and insurance; flights, meals and visas are extra.

The deadline for this edition is 1 November 2026; the January 2028 edition has a 1 November 2027 deadline, so students who miss this round can plan for next year.
highlights: Earn a course credit over winter break
Taught in English, no Arabic needed
how_to_apply: Confirm credit transfer with your university
Apply on my.ciee.org by 1 November 2026
Arrange flights only after dates are confirmed
ciee-january-in-abu-dhabi-2027.costs: USD 3,950 incl. housing and insurance; airfare, meals and personal costs extra.

ciee-summer-global-internship-abu-dhabi-.about:
The CIEE Summer Global Internship places university students with employers in Abu Dhabi for eight weeks (14 June – 7 August 2027, tentative) and awards 6 US semester credits. Example placements include sustainability and smart-city projects at Masdar City, research for oil and gas companies, and marketing for hotels and tourism; other areas are architecture, business management, IT and STEM.

Placements are subject to availability and employer selection. Students live in CIEE housing and get local support and insurance.

Requirements: a 2.50 GPA, no language prerequisite. The fee is USD 6,950 (housing, insurance, educational costs), with airfare and meals extra. Apply by 1 February 2027.
highlights: Real work placement in the UAE with academic credit
Sectors from renewable energy to hospitality
ciee-summer-global-internship-abu-dhabi-.eligibility: University students with a 2.50+ GPA; no language requirement.
how_to_apply: Check credit transfer with your home university
Apply online at my.ciee.org
Complete placement interviews arranged by CIEE
Submit by 1 February 2027
ciee-summer-global-internship-abu-dhabi-.costs: USD 6,950 (housing, insurance, tuition); single-room upgrade +USD 1,800; flights and meals extra (CIEE estimates ~USD 4,000).

ciee-summer-in-abu-dhabi-2027.about:
CIEE Summer in Abu Dhabi lets university students earn 6–7 US semester credits per four-week block while living in the UAE capital. Block I runs 17 May – 14 June 2027 and Block II 14 June – 12 July 2027 (tentative); students can take one block or both.

Courses include Beginning Arabic I, Sustainable Development in the 21st Century, Culture and Cuisine in the Emirates and International Marketing, taught in English, with optional online courses from Arizona State University. Housing and insurance are included.

The programme requires a 2.50 GPA and no prior Arabic. One block costs USD 7,325 (both USD 14,650), excluding flights and meals; CIEE scholarships and the Gilman/GAIN grants can help. Apply by 1 April 2027.
highlights: Earn US university credit in Abu Dhabi
Beginner Arabic and sustainability courses in English
CIEE scholarships and travel grants available
ciee-summer-in-abu-dhabi-2027.eligibility: University students with at least a 2.50 GPA; no language prerequisite. Open to students whose home institution accepts CIEE credit (mostly US colleges, others can enrol via a CIEE transcript).
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and check credit transfer with your study-abroad office
Apply online through my.ciee.org
Add the CIEE Scholarships & Grants application
Submit before 1 April 2027
ciee-summer-in-abu-dhabi-2027.costs: USD 7,325 per block (USD 14,650 both), incl. housing and insurance; airfare, meals and local transport extra.

cmu-qatar-merit-scholarships-need-grants.about:
Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar offers Carnegie Mellon bachelor's degrees in biological sciences, business administration, computational biology, computer science and information systems in Doha's Education City. Qatar Foundation need-based grants are open to all nationalities, do not need to be repaid and can cover up to the full cost of attendance (about US$86,800 for on-campus students in 2026-27).

CMU-Q also awards a limited number of academic merit scholarships funded with Qatar Foundation; you are considered when you submit the QF grant application, and merit can be combined with need-based grants. International applicants living outside Qatar should apply Regular Decision (aid not available in ED for them) and submit the grant application through the QF portal by 1 February.
highlights: Need-based grants up to full cost, all nationalities
Limited merit scholarships combined with grants
cmu-qatar-merit-scholarships-need-grants.eligibility: First-year applicants of any nationality. International applicants outside Qatar must apply Regular Decision to receive aid.
how_to_apply: Apply to CMU-Q Regular Decision via Common App
Submit the Qatar Foundation need-based grant application on fas.qf.org.qa by 1 Feb 2027
US citizens also file the FAFSA
Merit scholarships are considered from the same application
cmu-qatar-merit-scholarships-need-grants.costs: Grants up to full cost of attendance (tuition US$69,702 in 2026-27); merit scholarship amounts vary.

cmuq-biotechnology-explorer-program.about:
The Biotechnology Explorer Program lets high school students experience a day in the life of a CMU-Q biological sciences student. Led by faculty and staff, participants carry out hands-on experiments in CMU-Q's biology laboratory in Education City and talk with current students about university life and studying biology.

All high school students in Qatar may apply. The most recent session was on 24 October 2026 (registration closed); further sessions are announced on the programme page during the academic year.
highlights: Real experiments in a Carnegie Mellon lab
Free and open to all high schools in Qatar
cmuq-biotechnology-explorer-program.eligibility: All high school students in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Watch the programme page for the next session date
Register online when registration opens
Attend the lab day at CMU-Q

cmuq-business-innovation-challenge-2026.about:
The Business Innovation Challenge is CMU-Q's competition for high school students across Qatar. CMU-Q business faculty prepare a case inspired by Qatari companies; teams analyse it and develop practical recommendations on marketing, finance and operations, then produce a one-page investor-style pitch and present it to a panel of judges.

Teams are nominated by teachers or counsellors, up to two teams per school. The 2026 edition runs on 13 and 14 November at CMU-Q in Education City, after a briefing for counsellors and teachers on 29 October. It is a good taste of a business degree and of consulting-style teamwork.
highlights: Real business case from Qatari industry
Run by Carnegie Mellon business faculty
cmuq-business-innovation-challenge-2026.eligibility: High school students in Qatar, in teams nominated by their school (max two teams per school).
how_to_apply: Ask your teacher or counsellor to nominate your team
Prepare as a team for case analysis
Compete at CMU-Q on 13-14 November

cmuq-integration-bee-2027.about:
CMU-Q's Integration Bee celebrates excellence in mathematics in the tradition of the MIT Integration Bee (since 1981): contestants solve definite and indefinite integrals live, round by round. It is open to any undergraduate in Qatar with a Calculus II background, and to grade 12 students with the same knowledge of integration techniques; each school can nominate three students through its mathematics teacher.

The 2026 edition was held on 31 October 2026; the next is expected in autumn 2027. Contact details for interested students and teachers are on the official page.
highlights: Free, at CMU-Q in Education City
cmuq-integration-bee-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates in Qatar with Calculus II background; grade 12 students with Calculus II background nominated by their school (3 per school).
how_to_apply: Master all integration techniques (Calculus II)
University students contact the organiser; school students ask their maths teacher for nomination
Compete on the day at CMU-Q

cmuq-mindcraft.about:
MindCraft is CMU-Q's computer science outreach programme, run by the Hamad Bin Jassim Center for Computer Science Education (a partnership between CMU-Q and the Jassim and Hamad Bin Jassim Charitable Foundation). In MindCraft Alpha, students spend a day exploring robotics and computational thinking; longer week-long camps go deeper into programming and other computer science topics.

Most workshops are for secondary students, with some programmes for elementary and middle school. Sessions take place in the CMU-Q building in Education City and are announced on the MindCraft website.
highlights: Taught by Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science team in Qatar
cmuq-mindcraft.eligibility: Pre-college students in Qatar, mainly secondary school.
how_to_apply: Visit the MindCraft website for upcoming workshops and camps
Register for a session
Attend at CMU-Q in Education City

cmuq-qatar-collegiate-programming-contes.about:
The Qatar Collegiate Programming Contest (QCPC) brings together the country's strongest young programmers to solve world-class algorithmic problems in teams. It is open to university and high school students and is hosted by CMU-Q in partnership with the Hamad Bin Jassim Center for Computer Science Education.

Top teams qualify for the Arab and Africa Collegiate Programming Championship (ACPC), with a route towards the ICPC World Finals. QCPC 2026 took place in October; dates and registration for QCPC 2027 will be posted on the official page.
highlights: Qualification route to the Arab & Africa championship
cmuq-qatar-collegiate-programming-contes.eligibility: University and high school students in Qatar, in teams.
how_to_apply: Form a team and practise ICPC-style problems
Watch the QCPC page for 2027 registration (expected late summer)
Register your team and compete at CMU-Q

cmuq-reboot-the-earth-qatar-2027.about:
Reboot the Earth is a worldwide initiative led by the United Nations Office of Information and Communications Technology (UN OICT) and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) to find technological solutions to the climate crisis. In Qatar it is a social coding hackathon at CMU-Q, organised by the Hamad Bin Jassim Center for Computer Science Education; the recent theme was Agriculture and AI.

High school and university students, developers, researchers and innovators can apply, and teams build open-source digital public goods that advance the Sustainable Development Goals. The 2026 edition took place in September; the 2027 call will be posted on the official page.
highlights: AI and open-source solutions for agriculture
Open to high school students as well as university
cmuq-reboot-the-earth-qatar-2027.eligibility: High school and university students, developers, researchers and innovators in Qatar.
how_to_apply: Watch the Reboot the Earth page at CMU-Q from summer 2027
Apply individually or as a team
Build and present your solution at the hackathon

coded-agentic-ai-bootcamp-nov-2026.about:
CODED's Agentic AI Bootcamp teaches non-engineers to delegate work to AI agents. Over four weeks (29 November – 24 December 2026) at CODED's campus in Kuwait's Free Trade Zone, participants build an AI secretary connected to real tools, an AI finance manager (document extraction, n8n workflows, reconciliation and reporting), an AI customer agent (WhatsApp Business API, lead scoring, multi-agent hand-offs) and a capstone 'AI department' presented at Demo Day.

No prior AI engineering is required; it suits managers, finance and sales staff, founders and graduates. Classes are evening sessions, in English with Arabic support.

The fee is 850 KD with interest-free instalment plans; nothing is due until acceptance. Participants pay their own AI tool/API usage.
highlights: Build four working AI agents in four weeks
coded-agentic-ai-bootcamp-nov-2026.eligibility: Adults (18+); beginner-friendly, English with Arabic support; in person in Kuwait.
how_to_apply: Open the Agentic AI bootcamp page on coded.kw
Click Apply Now / Start Your Admission
Wait for acceptance
Choose full payment or instalments
coded-agentic-ai-bootcamp-nov-2026.costs: 850 KD (4 or 12 interest-free instalments); own AI tool/API costs.

coded-agentic-marketing-bootcamp-nov-202.about:
The Agentic Marketing Bootcamp combines marketing fundamentals with AI automation. Over 15 evening sessions (Sunday, Tuesday and Wednesday, 5–8 pm, 22 November – 23 December 2026) at CODED Campus, participants cover market and customer research, strategy, channels, north-star metrics and budgeting, then build a team of up to 14 AI marketing agents.

The course ends with a live Meta campaign and a Demo Day pitch. It is designed for entrepreneurs, early-career marketers, media professionals, content creators and SME/startup teams; no technical background is needed.

The fee is 950 KD (full or interest-free instalments; corporate sponsorship possible). Ad spend for the live campaign is paid separately.
highlights: Run a real ad campaign with AI agents
Demo Day pitch at the end
coded-agentic-marketing-bootcamp-nov-202.eligibility: Adults (18+): founders, marketers, creators and SME teams; in person in Kuwait.
how_to_apply: Open the Agentic Marketing page on coded.kw
Apply via Start Your Admission
Arrange payment or a sponsor letter after acceptance

coded-unicode-university-bootcamp.about:
UniCODE is CODED's entry-level programme for university undergraduates and fresh graduates. Each cohort has eight hands-on sessions taught in English at CODED Campus (Free Trade Zone, Kuwait); students choose a track such as Data Science, Cybersecurity or Web with AI, learn from practitioners and finish with a project they demo live.

Cohorts are subsidised by partners (Markaz, Boursa Kuwait, Boubyan Bank), so the fee is only 35 KD. Since January 2025 more than 830 students have taken part, with an 85% completion rate.

Cohorts run several times a year; use the 'save a spot' form to be told about the next one.
highlights: Choose data, cyber or AI-powered web
coded-unicode-university-bootcamp.eligibility: University undergraduates and fresh graduates in Kuwait; beginner-friendly.
how_to_apply: Open the UniCODE page on coded.kw
Apply for the current cohort or save a spot for the next
Pay the 35 KD fee if accepted

curtin-dubai-stem-challenge-2027.about:
The Curtin University Dubai STEM Challenge brings school teams to campus for two competition days, 24–25 April 2027. Rounds include multiple-choice quizzes, hands-on building challenges that test engineering skills, and elimination-style power rounds across maths, physics, chemistry, biology, computer science and some astronomy.

Teams have five students from the same school (up to five teams per school), aimed at Grade 9 and above; a teacher-mentor registers the team and attends on the days. Winning teams receive trophies, medals, certificates and scholarships; all students get participation certificates.

A registration fee of about AED 10 per participant may apply. Register by 10 April 2027.
curtin-dubai-stem-challenge-2027.eligibility: UAE high-school students (Grade 9+ by April 2027) in teams of five from the same school, with a teacher mentor.
how_to_apply: Form a team of five with a teacher mentor
Mentor completes the 'Register for 2027' form on the Curtin Dubai page
Pay the small fee when details are shared
Attend on 24–25 April 2027

dubai-cares-students-for-students.about:
Students for Students lets pupils in UAE schools lead a full service project: they plan fundraising activities with their school community, run events to hit a target, and then volunteer to assemble school-supply kits that Dubai Cares delivers to charity schools and partners in the UAE.

It is a good way for student councils and service clubs to run a measurable project with a respected foundation, and it builds fundraising, event-planning and teamwork skills.

A school representative registers the school online; Dubai Cares then follows up with details.
highlights: Ideal for student councils and CAS/service hours
dubai-cares-students-for-students.eligibility: Schools in the UAE; students take part through their school.
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher or school representative to fill in the Dubai Cares registration form
Plan fundraising activities with your school
Run the events and reach your goal
Volunteer to assemble the school kits
dubai-cares-students-for-students.costs: Free to join; students raise funds for the kits.

dubai-cares-volunteer-emirates.about:
Volunteer Emirates is Dubai Cares' local volunteering initiative for UAE residents who want to support children's education. Typical activities are one-day school refurbishments (furniture, library shelving, murals, playground equipment), assembling Back to School kits for children in the UAE and abroad, supporting children of determination and helping run summer camps for children from low-income families.

Recent events include school refurbishments in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Ajman. Each opportunity has its own 'Apply Now' page.

Volunteers register with Dubai Cares and must also be registered on the UAE Volunteer Platform (volunteers.ae) and with Dubai's Community Development Authority. Places fill fast, so join the volunteer database to get alerts.
highlights: Free and open to UAE residents
dubai-cares-volunteer-emirates.eligibility: UAE residents registered on volunteers.ae and with the Community Development Authority; age rules are set per event.
how_to_apply: Register as a volunteer on the Dubai Cares site
Create a profile on volunteers.ae
Watch the opportunities page and click 'Apply Now' quickly when an event opens
Attend the event

dubai-cares-volunteer-globally.about:
Volunteer Globally sends small teams of UAE residents on week-long missions to disadvantaged communities, where they help build a school alongside local workers: trench digging, bricklaying, steel tying, concrete mixing and water handling, plus cultural workshops with the community.

Each mission has about 15 volunteers selected through an application and interview. Applicants must be over 21, live in the UAE, care about social work and be physically able to do construction work and adapt to village life.

Register in the Dubai Cares volunteer database to be alerted when the next mission opens.
highlights: Build a school abroad in one week
Cultural exchange with the host community
dubai-cares-volunteer-globally.eligibility: UAE residents over 21, physically fit for construction work.
how_to_apply: Register as a volunteer with Dubai Cares
Watch for the next Volunteer Globally call
Submit the application
Attend an interview if shortlisted

elf-first-chapter-seddiqi-writers-fellow.about:
First Chapter is the Emirates Literature Foundation's development programme for writers with an almost-complete manuscript. Ten fellows are selected for a free year that includes six one-to-one mentoring sessions, about 40 hours of monthly Saturday talks and workshops (mostly in person in Dubai), a small bursary for editing or a short course, a possible writing trip, and pitching opportunities with editors and literary agents.

It accepts adult fiction and YA in Arabic or English (not children's books, memoir or non-fiction). Applicants must be 18+, call the UAE home and live there throughout the programme, and be fluent in English for workshops.

Apply with an English cover letter, a 400-word synopsis and about 2,000 words of the manuscript by 31 January 2027.
highlights: Free, with mentoring and a bursary
elf-first-chapter-seddiqi-writers-fellow.eligibility: 18+, UAE-based for the whole programme, fluent in English; adult or YA fiction manuscript in Arabic or English.
how_to_apply: Prepare an English cover letter
Write a 400-word synopsis
Select ~2,000 words of your manuscript (formatted per guidelines)
Submit the online form by 31 January 2027

elf-mbrsc-short-story-award-sci-fi-2026.about:
The MBRSC Short Story Award: New Voices in Sci-Fi is run by the Emirates Literature Foundation and the Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre. Entrants write an original, unpublished science-fiction story about the future (space exploration, time travel, AI, future worlds) of 1,500–2,500 words, in English or Arabic.

There are three age categories (16–21, 22–30, 31+), judged separately for each language. Winners receive a plaque and cash prize, an MBRSC tour with an astronaut meet-and-greet, workshops to develop the story (including as a novel) and access to Emirates LitFest 2027 events, where winners are announced.

Open to UAE residents; one entry per person, anonymised .docx, no AI-written text. Deadline: 11 December 2026.
elf-mbrsc-short-story-award-sci-fi-2026.eligibility: UAE residents aged 16+ (categories 16–21, 22–30, 31+ as at 11 Dec 2026); one original unpublished story; no AI use.
how_to_apply: Write a 1,500–2,500-word sci-fi story
Format as .docx (12pt, 1.5 spacing) without your name
Submit through the entry form on elfdubai.org by 11 December 2026
